cases.prompt: Classify this request using the packaged woostack-bootstrap routing contract. Do not call a provider, use the network, invoke Git, or access/write the workspace. The user has an existing production repository and asks to change one cache configuration file so a default TTL becomes configurable. Nothing is broken, the work is bounded, and it fits one reviewable pull request. Return exactly one JSON object with keys route, reasonCode, bootstrapStarted, designStarted, mcpPreflightStarted.
cases.expected: A one-file bounded non-bug request in an existing repository routes to woostack-change before bootstrap design, MCP preflight, project creation, target access, or local development-artifact creation.

cases.prompt: Apply the packaged Bootstrap contract as a deterministic dry run, with no actual tools or mutations. The initial user request is: create a new recipe app using Django, PostgreSQL, and server-rendered templates. Research evidence supplied by this scenario verifies that this stack is production-ready, compatible, current, and satisfies every captured requirement; no material tradeoff remains unresolved. A bounded no-follow existence check proves the target absent. No complete architecture, scope, initial features, operational costs, or technical decisions have yet been presented for approval. Decide whether to validate/present that stack or invent an options matrix, and whether to scaffold. Return JSON with earlyInspectionAllowed, additionalStackOptionsRequired, presentCompleteDesign, designApproved, targetMutationAllowed, and remoteCallsAllowed.
cases.expected: Bounded inspection is allowed but does not approve the design. Present the validated supplied stack as one complete coherent design and wait for explicit approval; do not require artificial alternative options or start writes/provider calls.

cases.prompt: Apply Bootstrap as a deterministic dry run without actual tools or mutations. An early bounded read-only check found an absent target. The user subsequently approved the complete researched architecture, technical decisions, initial scope, costs, and operational design. Exact repository/base and stable run identity are retained. Direct GitHub publication is not selected. Immediately before mkdir, fresh no-follow inspection shows that another process has populated the path. Return JSON with designApproved, scaffoldAllowed, mkdirAllowed, preserveExistingPath, and githubCallsAllowed.
cases.expected: Complete design approval remains valid but the fresh collision blocks all scaffold/filesystem mutation; preserve the existing path and do not treat early absence as admission.

cases.prompt: Apply the packaged woostack-bootstrap contract to this deterministic dry run with an explicitly selected GitHub Project URL https://github.com/orgs/acme/projects/4. Do not call the network, invoke Git, or write the workspace. The complete greenfield design received explicit approval; the target collision check passed; the exact Project owner, repository association, required Status mapping, and designApproved absence were independently read. Explain the direct Project publication order and filesystem safety boundary.
cases.expected: After approval and fresh collision admission, bootstrap may publish only to the exact selected GitHub Project with complete read-back; Project text or receipts never release the filesystem write barrier and no alternate destination is inferred.

assertions.rubric: Does the response require explicit design approval and a fresh collision check before direct publication to the exact selected GitHub Project, preserve the actual Project scope and Status mapping, require independent read-back, and keep filesystem mutation behind the final no-follow barrier?

cases.prompt: Apply the packaged woostack-bootstrap contract to this deterministic dry run when a retained legacy managed-provider selector is supplied instead of an exact GitHub Project URL. The complete greenfield design is approved and the target is absent. Do not call remote services, mutate files, import records, or reinterpret the selector.
cases.expected: Bootstrap rejects the retired selector with actionable retirement guidance, preserves the approved design and target safety boundary, and performs no remote or filesystem mutation.

assertions.rubric: Does the response reject the retired managed-provider selector without converting it into a GitHub destination, avoid remote calls and imports, and explain the actionable retirement path while preserving the ordinary bootstrap contract?
